questions.stem: Uranium-238 (atomic number 92) undergoes alpha decay. What are the mass number and atomic number of the daughter nucleus?
questions.explanation: In alpha decay, an alpha particle (mass number 4, atomic number 2) is emitted. The daughter nucleus has: mass number = 238 - 4 = 234, and atomic number = 92 - 2 = 90. Option A subtracts 2 from mass and 1 from atomic number (confusing alpha with another decay). Option C does not change the mass number. Option D does not change the atomic number. Both mass number and atomic number must decrease in alpha decay.

questions.stem: Carbon-14 (atomic number 6) undergoes beta decay. What is the atomic number of the daughter nucleus?
questions.explanation: In beta decay, a neutron in the nucleus converts into a proton and an electron (beta particle). The beta particle is emitted, so the number of protons increases by 1: atomic number goes from 6 to 7 (nitrogen). The mass number stays the same (14) because a neutron is replaced by a proton (both have mass number 1). A common error is thinking the atomic number decreases (B) or stays the same (C).

questions.stem: In the nuclear equation: Ra-226 (atomic number 88) -> Rn-X (atomic number Y) + alpha particle, what are the values of X and Y?
questions.explanation: An alpha particle has mass number 4 and atomic number 2. Conservation requires: mass numbers balance: 226 = X + 4, so X = 222. Atomic numbers balance: 88 = Y + 2, so Y = 86. Option B subtracts 2 from mass and 1 from atomic number. Option C subtracts 4 from the atomic number instead of 2. Option D adds instead of subtracting.

questions.stem: Gamma emission often occurs alongside alpha or beta decay. When a nucleus emits only a gamma ray, what happens to its mass number and atomic number?

options.text: Mass number decreases by 4, atomic number decreases by 2
Mass number stays the same, atomic number increases by 1
Both mass number and atomic number remain unchanged
Mass number decreases by 1, atomic number stays the same

questions.explanation: Gamma rays are electromagnetic radiation with no mass and no charge. When a nucleus emits a gamma ray, it loses energy but neither its mass number nor its atomic number changes -- the nucleus remains the same isotope, just in a lower energy state. Option A describes alpha decay. Option B describes beta decay. Option D describes neutron emission.

questions.stem: A nucleus of thorium-232 (atomic number 90) undergoes two successive alpha decays. What is the mass number and atomic number of the resulting nucleus?
questions.explanation: Each alpha decay reduces the mass number by 4 and the atomic number by 2. After two alpha decays: mass number = 232 - 4 - 4 = 224, atomic number = 90 - 2 - 2 = 86. Option A shows only one alpha decay. Option C gets the mass right but the atomic number wrong. Option D gets the mass wrong but the atomic number right. For multiple decays, apply each change sequentially.
